nameStory: The Red-footed Longhorn Beetle gets its name from two standout features that make it easy to remember. Like all longhorn beetles, it sports impressively long antennae that can stretch as long as or longer than its entire body, resembling the horns of a longhorn steer. The 'red-footed' part comes from its distinctively colored legs that contrast beautifully with its metallic blue-green body.
description: The Red-footed Longhorn Beetle is a striking metallic beetle that catches the eye with its jewel-like appearance. Its body shimmers with blue-green iridescence, while its legs display warm reddish-orange tones that give it its common name. Like all longhorn beetles, it has remarkably long antennae and a somewhat elongated body shape. These beetles are medium-sized members of their family, with adults typically measuring around half an inch to three-quarters of an inch in length.

idTips.label: Metallic blue-green body
idTips.description: The body gleams with an unmistakable metallic blue-green sheen that shifts slightly in different light, feeling smooth and hard to the touch like polished metal

idTips.label: Reddish-orange legs
idTips.description: All six legs display warm reddish-orange coloration that contrasts dramatically with the cool-toned metallic body

idTips.label: Extra-long antennae
idTips.description: Thread-like antennae extend as long as or longer than the beetle's body, constantly moving and feeling around as the beetle explores

idTips.label: Elongated body shape
idTips.description: The body is noticeably longer than it is wide, with a somewhat cylindrical shape typical of longhorn beetles

idTips.label: Hard wing covers
idTips.description: The wing covers (elytra) feel rigid and smooth, completely covering the hindwings when at rest

habitat: Red-footed Longhorn Beetles are found in deciduous and mixed forests throughout New England, particularly where dead and dying hardwood trees provide breeding sites. Look for adults on flowers and foliage in forest clearings, woodland edges, and areas with a mix of mature trees and younger growth. They're often associated with oak, maple, and other native hardwoods where their larvae develop in decaying wood.

seasonality.spring: Adults begin emerging in late spring as temperatures warm, becoming active on sunny days when they start seeking flowers for nectar feeding.
seasonality.summer: Peak activity period when adults are most commonly seen visiting flowers during the day and are attracted to lights at night. This is the best time for observation.
seasonality.fall: Adult activity winds down as cooler weather sets in, though some individuals may still be seen on warm autumn days before going dormant.
seasonality.winter: Adults are dormant and hidden under bark, in leaf litter, or other protected locations. Larvae continue developing slowly inside dead wood.

funFact: Despite their intimidating long antennae and metallic armor-like appearance, these beetles are actually flower visitors with a sweet tooth, spending much of their adult lives sipping nectar like tiny, jeweled hummingbirds of the insect world.
confusionNotes: The metallic blue-green body with contrasting red-orange legs makes this species quite distinctive among New England longhorns, but other metallic longhorn beetles might cause confusion. Remember the simple rule: blue-green body plus red feet equals Red-footed Longhorn - no other common longhorn in our region has this exact color combination.
contextualKnowledge: Like many longhorn beetles, this species plays an important ecological role as both a decomposer (larvae break down dead wood) and pollinator (adults visit flowers for nectar). The family name Cerambycidae comes from a Greek word meaning 'horn,' referring to their characteristic long antennae.
compareHints: As the only Anthophylax species in New England, the Red-footed Longhorn stands apart from other metallic longhorns in the region by its specific blue-green and red-orange color pattern. While other longhorn beetles may show metallic coloration, none combine the bright metallic blue-green body with distinctly reddish legs in quite the same way. Most similar metallic longhorns are either uniformly colored or have different color combinations entirely.
